Here's the page. The bits in square brackets are for you to fill in.

# Helping your midwife find you

Hello from your Riverside community midwives.

My name is [your name] and I am one of your midwives. I am good at catching babies. I am not so good at finding houses. The team asked me to write this page because I am the one who gets lost the most, so I know all the ways it can go wrong.

When your baby is coming at 3am, we want to be in your house fast. Here is how you can help us. None of it is hard, and most of it you can do weeks before.

## When to phone, and who to phone

**From 37 weeks:** when you think labour has started, phone the Riverside birth line on **[birth line number]**, day or night. The line goes to the midwife who is on call.

Please do not phone or text a midwife's own mobile, even if you have the number and even if she is your favourite. She might be asleep or on holiday.

**Before 37 weeks:** home birth cover has not started yet, so your care is at the hospital. Phone the maternity unit on **[hospital number]** and go in. We tell everybody this at the booking visit and everybody forgets, so here it is again.

When you phone the birth line, please tell us:

- your name and full address, with the postcode
- your flat number and the name of your building, if you live in a flat
- anything tricky about finding you or getting in

Save the birth line number in your phone today. Put it in your birth partner's phone too, because they will probably be the one who phones.

## Send us a pin

A pin on the map is better than any directions. You can do it two ways:

- Open WhatsApp and send your location to the birth line phone.
- Use what3words. It is a free app that gives every small square of ground its own three words. Find the square at your front door and tell us the three words.

Try it once before labour starts. It's much harder to learn a new app in the middle of a contraction.

## Make your house easy to spot

**Show your number.** Check that we can see your house number from the road. If your house has a name and no number, please tell us which houses you are between. I once looked for "Rosemary Cottage" in a long street of terraces. The sat nav took me to a chippy. There was no baby at the chippy.

**Flats need extra directions.** Tell us the building name, which entrance to use, which floor, and the buzzer number. I once drove round a block of flats in Everton for 20 minutes. Flat 14 was not next to flat 13. It was in the other building. In the end the dad waved a tea towel out of the window, and that is how I found them.

**Porch light on, please.** At night in winter, dark streets all look the same. Turn on the porch light, or the light in the front room with the curtains open.

**Give us a sign.** One family tied balloons to the gate, like for a party. Best idea ever, I found them straight away. Balloons, a tea towel, a person waving in a dressing gown, anything like that helps.

**Watch the door for us.** If someone can look out for us, even better. I once walked into the wrong house because the front door was open. A nice old man gave me a Jammie Dodger anyway. He was very kind, but he was not having a baby.

## Parking

Two midwives come to your birth, and we usually come in two cars. If you can keep two spaces free near your door, we will love you for it. Maybe ask a neighbour, or move your own car down the road.

We carry a lot. There are gas and air cylinders, the big bag, and sometimes birthing pool things too. The shorter the walk, the less tired our arms are when we get to you.

**Permit zones.** Lots of streets round Anfield and Kensington are permit parking. If yours is one, ask the council for visitor permits before 37 weeks and keep them by the front door, ready for our dashboards. We have had parking tickets before while a baby was being born, and it spoils a lovely night.

## Inside your home

**Clear the hallway and stairs.** Please move the shoes, the washing basket and the Lego. When I am carrying the big bag I cannot see my feet, and Lego hurts even more at 3am.

**Pets in another room.** I love dogs, I really do. But there was a staffie called Pippin who loved me too much. She jumped on me at every visit, and one time I nearly dropped the gas and air. So when you phone the birth line, please put your pets in another room with the door shut. They can meet the baby afterwards.

## If you can't do something on this list

Don't worry. Maybe there is no parking on your street, or the porch light is broken, or your building is a maze. Just tell us when you phone and we will work it out together. We are not going to tell you off.

## Fridge checklist

Cut this out and stick it on the fridge.

**Before 37 weeks**

☐ Birth line number saved in my phone: [birth line number]

☐ Birth line number saved in my birth partner's phone

☐ Hospital number saved too, for before 37 weeks: [hospital number]

☐ I have tried sending a WhatsApp pin, or I know my what3words

☐ House number is easy to see from the road

☐ Directions for flats written down (building, entrance, floor, buzzer)

☐ Visitor parking permits ready by the front door, if we live in a permit zone

☐ Porch light works

**When labour starts**

☐ Phone the Riverside birth line, not a midwife's own mobile

☐ Send the pin or the three words

☐ Porch light on, if it is dark

☐ Balloons, tea towel or a waving person at the front

☐ Two parking spaces kept free, if possible

☐ Hallway and stairs clear

☐ Pets in another room, door shut

☐ Someone watching the door for us

## One last thing

I am from the Philippines, and there we say the midwife is like family. That is how we want you to think of us. Help us find you, and we will be there as quick as we can.

See you soon,

[your name] and all the Riverside community midwives

Before it goes in the pack:

- **Hospital number:** your notes only said that before 37 weeks they go to the hospital, so I added a line to phone the maternity unit first. Check with Deb that this is right.
- **Extra advice:** I added a few small things that were not in your notes, such as what to say on the phone, the buzzer number for flats, and asking a neighbour about parking. Take out anything that doesn't fit how your team works.
